text:
Person: Please turn on the porch camera and tell me if anyone rang the bell today.
Assistant: Sure. Which camera do you mean, the front porch or the back door?
Person: The front porch. I'm in the laundry room and the washer is so loud I can't hear a thing.
Assistant: Got it. The front porch camera is on and it works well. The bell rang twice today, once at nine and once at noon.
Person: Good. Lock the back door and set the alarm too.
Assistant: The back door is locked. What time should the alarm start tonight?
Person: Ten o'clock, please.

A phrase app helps you say simple things in another language, like asking where the park is or how much a ticket costs. People use it when they travel, or when they are tired of looking up words one at a time. You can change the language, slow the voice down, or save a phrase to a list. You might say, "say it again slower," or "switch to Spanish," or "what does this word mean?" Learning a language is a bit like making soup: you stir in a few new words every day, and slowly they mix together. Spelling help works the same way. Ask how to spell a word and the assistant says it letter by letter.

Sam woke up bored and slow. A bird sat on the fence outside, singing at nothing. His phone was on the pillow, so he picked it up and mumbled, "Show tasks." The assistant understood that he wanted his to-do list for today and read it out: pay the water bill, call Aunt Rosa, and fix the shelf. Sam yawned. "Bill's paid." The assistant understood that the water bill was already done, so it checked that task off the list. Then Sam said, "Count what's left," and the assistant told him two tasks were left. Sam smiled, because two tasks felt easy, and he got out of bed.

Priya woke up to her phone buzzing again and again. Every few seconds it showed a new like on her photo of the cake she baked. She rubbed her eyes and said, "Stop telling me about every like, but don't turn off messages from my sister." The assistant understood that she did not want like alerts, but she did want to keep messages from her sister. It turned off the like notifications and left the sister messages on. A minute later the phone was quiet. Then a friend's post, written in big capital letters, seemed to shout about cheap concert tickets. Priya smiled and saved the post for later, since she was finally awake.

An automatic pet feeder gives your cat or dog food at the same times every day. It is useful when you are at work or away for the weekend. People often change how much food comes out, or when the meal happens. They might say, "give him a bit less at night," or "feed her at seven instead of eight." The feeder can also record each meal, so you can check later that the bowl was filled. Some people put the bowl on a rug so the floor stays clean. If a pet seems too full or too hungry, you can ask for a smaller or bigger portion.

Mia was lying on a towel at the beach with her phone. She typed, "ugh the sun is so strong and my nose is already pink." The assistant understood that she was getting sunburnt and needed sun cream. It said it could set a reminder to put on more every two hours, and Mia said yes. It also told her the tide would fall in about an hour, so there would be a pretty strip of sand to walk on. Mia found her missing sock under the towel and laughed. When the reminder buzzed two hours later, she put on more sun cream and moved under the umbrella.

Ben sat at his desk with a messy pile of papers and a cold coffee. He said to his phone, "Read me the top headlines and tell me the score of last night's game." The assistant understood that he wanted two things, so it did both. First it read three headlines: one about a new bridge, one about an artist who would paint a big picture of the ocean on a school wall, and one about the weather. Then it said the home team had won by two points. Ben nodded, thanked the assistant, and went back to sorting his papers while it read the next headline.

Lena woke up in a humid bedroom on a slow afternoon. The fan was not helping. She grabbed her phone and typed fast, in lowercase: "open my book and go to the bookmrak." The assistant understood that bookmrak meant bookmark. It opened her book on the page she had saved, chapter nine. Lena then asked it to call her a good time to stop reading, and the assistant said she usually read for thirty minutes, so it set a gentle timer. Lena lay back with the book, and when the timer rang she put the bookmark back in and went to find a cold drink.

Person: Did my package come today? I'm so tired after work.
Assistant: I can check. Which package do you mean?
Person: The blue one. Wait, no, the one from the shoe website.
Assistant: Okay, the shoe website order. It says it was delivered at ten this morning and left by the front door.
Person: Good. I paid for express shipping, so I'm glad it came quickly.
Assistant: Yes, it came a day early. The porch light flashed when the driver left it there.
Person: Thanks. Can you sign for the next one for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't sign for packages. But I can tell you when one arrives.

Tom was eight and he was going camping on Saturday. He had a little cough, so his mom let him ask the speaker for help. "Tell me what to pack for the tent and what the weather will be on the hill," he said. The assistant understood that he wanted two things. It read a short packing list: a warm jacket, a sleeping bag, a flashlight, and a water bottle. Because of the cough, it said to pack an extra scarf. Then it said the hill would be cool and dry on Saturday. Tom packed his gold flashlight first. He wanted to celebrate the trip with a big marshmallow.

Person: Please lock the door.
Assistant: Of course. Which door do you mean, the front door, the back door, or the garage?
Person: The garage. No wait, the front door. I took the trash out and left it open.
Assistant: The front door is locked now.
Person: Thank you. It was rude of me to leave it open when the neighbor came by.
Assistant: Don't worry. Do you want me to shut the garage door as well?
Person: Yes, please shut it.
Assistant: The garage door is shut.

Carlos was driving to work when he said, "Put on the news station." The assistant understood that he wanted the news on the radio and tuned in to the news channel. Carlos was a bit nervous about being late. A hammer rattled in the toolbox in the back seat, and he tried to ignore it. After a minute he said, "No, wait, the sports channel instead." The assistant understood that he had changed his mind, so it switched to the sports station. Carlos listened to the match talk, spot on time to hear the score. When he parked, he was happy to spot an empty space right by the door.

They want to know if this month's electricity bill is higher than last month's.
Is my bill more than last month?
Did the power bill go up?
How much more did I pay this time?
Text me the amount for this month and last month.
I think my hair dryer may have doubled the bill. Is it twice what it was?
Is the bill half of what it was in winter, or about the same?
Could you tell me if this month's electricity cost is less or more than before?
I'd like a fancy little chart that shows how much more I spent this month, if you don't mind.
Would you please compare this month's bill with last month's and tell me which one is bigger?

They want to find the note about their shopping list.
Shopping list.
Find my list.
Open shopping note.
Where is the note I made for groceries?
Show me what I wrote about the store.
The voice note I made when my phone beeped, the one with the milk and eggs.
I wrote something on a cloudy Monday about what to buy and what's in my purse. Can you find it?
Could you please look through my notes and open the one about groceries?

Dana was folding clothes with one hand and holding a spoon with the other. She called out, "Start the dryer and send me a message when it's done." The assistant understood that she wanted two things, so it started the dryer and said it would send a message when the cycle ended. Her son was watching an episode of his favorite show, and he opened his eyes wide when the dryer began to hum. Forty minutes later the phone buzzed with a message that the dryer was done. Dana put the spoon down, took out the warm clothes, and filled the wide basket again.

Grandpa Joe did not know much about his new gadgets. The little box by his bed was one of them. Last night he had woken up too early, so he said to it, "I want to sleep longer. Make my alarm half an hour later." The assistant understood that he wanted the alarm moved from seven to seven thirty, and it said so. Joe was glad. "And I'd like more deep sleep," he said. The assistant explained that it could not change how he slept, but it could remind him to go to bed earlier. Joe agreed. The next morning he slept until seven thirty and felt much better.

Nora had just finished a long night shift at the hospital. On the bus home she said to her phone, "Find out if the Thai place is open and book a table for two at seven." The assistant understood that she wanted two things. It checked the opening hours and found the restaurant was open until ten. Then it booked a table for two at seven. It also warned her that the place gets busy on weekends, so she should arrive a little early. Nora has a vegetarian diet, so she asked for the menu, and the assistant said there were many dishes she could eat. For dessert she wanted frozen yogurt. She smiled and closed her eyes.

Harold did not trust his phone much, but his hair was getting long. He was cutting bread with a knife in the kitchen when he said, "Book haircut." The assistant understood that he wanted an appointment at the barber. It asked, "Which day would you like?" Harold said, "Saturday morning." The assistant booked ten o'clock on Saturday and said the barber would welcome him at the shop on Elm Street. It also said the wait is usually short, with a maximum of fifteen minutes. Harold thanked it and finished his sandwich. On Saturday he walked in at ten, and the barber was ready for him.

Lily was nine and she lived a mile from the park. Her tomatoes were the thing she cared about most. Before school she told the speaker, "Water the plants tomorrow at seven." The assistant understood that she wanted the garden sprinkler to run at seven o'clock the next morning, and it said it had set that up. Lily also wanted to paint the fence blue, but she knew the paint needed to dry, so she asked the assistant if it would rain. It said no rain was coming. The next morning the sprinkler turned on at seven, and the tomatoes got a long drink while Lily ate breakfast.

Omar woke up and checked his phone before his eyes were fully open. "Where's my parcel?" he asked. The assistant understood that he wanted the tracking for his latest online order and told him the driver was about twenty-five minutes away. Omar said, "Forward that to my brother." The assistant sent the tracking message to his brother. The parcel was a pair of cinema tickets in a small envelope, a gift for his mom. The assistant said there might be a short delay on the road, but it would still come before noon. Omar got up, made tea, and waited by the door.

Person: Could you please set a timer for my card game? My grandchildren are coming on Friday, and I want every turn to be short so nobody gets bored.
Assistant: Happy to. How long should each turn be?
Person: Oh, I don't know. What do you think?
Assistant: Two minutes is a good start. Should I set it for two minutes?
Person: Yes. And can you tell me the current score?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't see your cards, so I don't know the score. If you tell me the points, I can keep them.
Person: Good idea. Please wipe the old score first.
Assistant: Done. The score is zero to zero.

Aisha got home from the hospital at dawn, tired and hungry. She was on a diet, so she poured a bowl of plain oats and sat in the dim kitchen. Then she remembered the old camera by the door and typed fast, in lowercase: "turn on the hallway camra." The assistant understood that she meant the hallway camera. It turned the camera on and said it was recording. She asked if a second one could be installed by the back door. The assistant said it could not install a camera by itself, but it could find a local shop and book a visit. Aisha said yes, and then she went to sleep.

Mark came home after a long day at the office and said, "Play some jazz on the kitchen speaker." The assistant understood that he wanted jazz in the kitchen and started a soft playlist there. A minute later Mark said, "Actually, the living room one." The assistant understood that he had changed his mind, so it stopped the music in the kitchen and moved it to the living room speaker. The room was dark, so Mark asked for the lamp to be turned on, and the assistant did that. On the other hand, he did not want it too loud, since he had invited a friend to talk. He asked for the volume to be lower, and the assistant lowered it.

They want the pool pump turned on.
Pump on.
Start the pool pump.
The water looks dim and cloudy. Can you get the pump going?
Switch the pool cleaner on, please.
I'd like the pump running before lunch.
My kids have swim practice in an hour. Can you start the pool pump?
Could you please turn on the pump now? We have a birthday party at the pool this afternoon, and I want the water to be clear before we bring out the cake.
Would you mind starting the pump so the water is clean and ready for our guests?

Jin ran out the door with a bag in one hand and his phone in the other. The assistant could hear him breathing fast. "Days left?" he asked. The assistant was not sure what he meant, so it said, "Days left until what?" Jin said, "My trip." The assistant knew his trip was on the calendar for next Tuesday. It answered that there were six days left. Jin said, "Message Dad." The assistant sent a text to his dad saying Jin would be there in six days. Jin read it online later on the train and was glad it had gone through.

Grace owns a small shop on a busy road. One morning she walked in and sniffed. "It smells dusty in here, and the air feels heavy," she said to the smart speaker. The assistant understood that she thought the air filter was old and needed a change. It asked if she wanted a repair visit, and Grace said yes. It found a digital booking page and set a visit for Thursday at nine. Grace wanted to know the price. The assistant told her the filter was forty dollars. She asked it to subtract the price from this week's repair budget, and the assistant told her what was left. Grace nodded and opened the shop.

A digital door lock works with a code, a phone, or a small card instead of a key. It is for people who forget keys, or who want to let a guest in while they are away. At a theater or an office, the same kind of lock lets only some people turn the handle and walk in. At home, people change the code, add a guest code for a day, or lock the door from far away. They might say, "lock the front door," "let my sister in," or "change the code to a new one." The lock can also tell you when the door was last opened.

They want to know the weather in the hills tonight.
Is it going to be chilly up there?
Will it get cold tonight in the hills?
How low will it go tonight?
Will it drop below ten degrees?
Should I bring a thick jacket for the hill camp?
I want to cook outside tonight. Will the wind be too strong?
Is it too chilly to put the carpet down in the tent and sleep?
Could you please tell me what the night weather will be like on the hill, so I know how many blankets to pack?

Rosa came in from walking the dog and hung the leash on the hook. The house felt dry and smelled of salty soup from last night. She said, "Turn on the air purifier and make the room a little less dry." The assistant understood that she wanted two things, so it switched on the purifier and started the humidifier. It said the air would feel better in about an hour. Her son said, "I like the humidifier, it sounds like rain." Rosa laughed. Then she asked the assistant to open the window in the kitchen for a few minutes, to let in fresh air. The assistant said it could not open windows, but it could remind her to do it.

Many board games and puzzles keep score or use a timer. A timer helps everyone know when a turn will end, and a score keeper helps players remember the points. Sometimes the rules seem weird, so people ask for them to be read out loud. They might say, "start a three minute timer," "give me ten more seconds," or "add five points to Sam." Some people also ask, "who is winning?" or "reset the score." An empty can or a plastic cup can hold game pieces, and a small bell can mark the end of a round. The fun part is that everyone agrees on the rules before they begin.

Grandpa Arthur stood at the bottom of the hill with his bike. His homework from the doctor was to ride a little every day, but his legs felt tired just looking at the hill. He told the speaker, "That hill looks like a mountain today." The assistant understood that he did not want a hard ride, so it found three routes and ranked them by how flat they were. The first was a small loop by the river, about five miles. Arthur chose that one. The assistant read the turns out loud, and he rode slowly, enjoying the trees. At the end he was a little tired, but he was glad he had gone.

They want to know what events are happening on their street this weekend.
Any local events?
What's on this weekend near me?
Something happening a step from my door?
Show me the community events for Saturday and Sunday.
Tell me about the street fair, and turn on a reminder for it.
Are there any medium sized events nearby, like a market or a concert in the park?
Find the events near my house this weekend and let me know which ones are free.
Could you please check the neighborhood board and tell me about the events, and also tell me if there is any noise warning for the weekend?

A car needs a little care to run well. Fuel and tyre pressure are the two things most people check. When a tyre feels soft, you add air; when a tyre cap is loose, you tighten it. Many people ask their assistant, "how much fuel is left?" or "are my tyres okay?" My grandfather used to say a car you can afford is one you can keep clean and check each week. Warming up the car on a cold morning is also common, so people say, "start the car in five minutes" or "warm it up to twenty degrees." Some ask, "where did I park?" and the car replies with the street.

Writing is how we put ideas on a page. A first draft is just a rough try, and editing is what you do later to fix it. Kids at school write stories, and grown-ups write emails and notes. People often ask a helper to check spelling, count the words, or make a sentence shorter. They might say, "how do you spell necessary?" or "how many words is this?" or "make this sound more polite." When a kid is stuck, they might click on a spelling tool to see the right word. It is pretty normal to change a sentence many times. Most good writing comes from drafting, reading it out loud, and fixing it again.

Kim came out of the hospital after a long night shift, feeling empty. A light rain fell on the forest of trees by the bus stop. She took out her phone and said, "Order dinner." The assistant asked, "From which place?" Kim said, "The usual." The assistant understood that she meant the noodle shop on Forest Road, where she ordered several times a week. It ordered her regular noodles and told her they would arrive in thirty minutes. Kim said, "Call me when it's close." The assistant said it would send a call when the driver was near. She sat on the bus and finally relaxed.

Person: I need to pay the electric bill.
Assistant: I can help with that. Which bill is it, and how much is it?
Person: Twenty-five dollars. I'm very tired after work, so please be quick.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't pay bills. But I can remind you of the date and the amount.
Person: That's fine. It's due on the tenth. I just bought some pork on the way home, and I forgot the date.
Assistant: Yes, it is due on the tenth. Should I remind you the day before?
Person: Yes, please. I got a message saying it was late, but that was a false alarm.
Assistant: Good. I'll remind you on the ninth.

name: bake_timer
does: Works out when to start each step of a bake and sets a timer, so bread and cakes come out kind and soft.
inputs: what you are baking, the oven temperature, and what time you want it ready
people say:
- When should the bread go in so it's done by six?
- My dough is ready. How long do I let it rise?
- Set a timer for the cookies, they burn if I forget.
- I think my mixer belt is slipping, so how long should I knead by hand?
- Tell me when the cake needs to come out.

Many people park their cars on a street and forget where they left them. A car helper can remember the place for you. On a street north of the market, for example, every car looks the same in the evening. People ask, "where is my car?" or "show me where I parked." The same helper can tell you if the car needs fuel or is covered in dust. You might say, "is it dirty?" or "remind me to wash it on Saturday." Some people also ask it to warm up the engine before they leave, or to tell them when the tyre pressure is low.

name: write_email_draft
does: Writes a first draft of an email in the tone you want, and can send a blind copy to people you choose.
inputs: who the email is for, what it should say, and the tone, like warm or formal
people say:
- Write a note to my boss saying I'll be late.
- Make it sound warm, not stiff.
- Send this to the team but hide everyone's addresses.
- Tell Anna thanks for the dinner, keep it short.
- Can you help me sound polite? I need to say no to a meeting.

name: pet_walk_planner
does: Plans a dog walk by picking a time and a route, and tells you how long the walk will take.
inputs: the pet's name, how long you want to walk, and the time of day
people say:
- Rex needs a walk this morning, but it might rain.
- Where can my dog swim near here?
- Plan a short walk, only twenty minutes.
- Pick a quiet route for my shy dog.
- Show me several places where dogs can run free.

Ravi owns a shop on the corner, and his hands were full of boxes. His pulse was fast from rushing around. He said to his phone, fast and in lowercase, "chekc off ordr stock and move paint to monday." The assistant understood that he had typed fast. It marked the stock order as done on his to-do list, and moved the paint task to Monday. The list felt strange to Ravi, because it was so short now. He asked the assistant to change the first item to top priority, and it did. Ravi smiled, picked up another box, and went to open the door for his first customer.

Amy was new to the city and lived on the north side. She sat on the porch with her baby, who was finally asleep. "Remind me to feed the baby at six," she said to the phone. The assistant set a reminder for six o'clock. Then Amy said, "No, wait, half past six. She ate late today." The assistant understood that she had changed her mind. It deleted the first reminder and set a new one for six thirty. Amy also asked when the baby's last nap had started, and the assistant told her it was at two. She put the phone down and watched the quiet street.

Person: Join the meeting.
Assistant: Which meeting do you mean? You have two today.
Person: The monthly one with Pat.
Assistant: Okay, joining the monthly meeting with Pat now.
Person: I can't hear well. Make it twice as loud.
Assistant: I made the sound louder. Is that better?
Person: Yes. Oh, sorry, I was eating lunch with a fork and my voice cracked.
Assistant: That's okay. Do you want me to share your screen too?
Person: Not yet, maybe later.

They want a reminder about their homework due date.
Remind me about homework.
Tell me when my work is due.
Can you ping me tomorrow at seven about the maths sheet?
I need a temporary reminder for Friday morning, just for the history essay.
After I bathe the dog tomorrow morning, tell me what homework is left.
What is due this week, and when?
Would you please remind me the night before my science project is due?
Could you please set a reminder for tomorrow morning at eight so I remember to hand in my book report before class?

Tony was a cook, and his left hand was covered in flour. His phone buzzed on the counter with a warning that the battery was low. He said, "Don't turn off the ringer, just make the screen dimmer." The assistant understood that he did not want the ringer silent, since he was waiting for a call from the delivery driver. It lowered the screen brightness and kept the ringer on. Tony asked it to speak the battery percentage, and it said, "Fifteen percent." He plugged the phone in next to the bags of rice on the shelf, high above the stove, at a height he could reach. Then he went back to making dough.

Person: Call Mary.
Assistant: Which Mary? You have Mary Smith and Mary from the clinic.
Person: My daughter.
Assistant: Mary Smith, then. Calling her now.
Person: Wait. Can you lend me your voice so I can say hello to my grandson in the grade school choir?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't lend my voice to other people. But I can send him a short message from you. What should it say?
Person: Tell him I'm proud of him. And that his tiny singing voice is the best.
Assistant: I'll send that to him.

They want the steps to make pancakes.
Pancake steps.
How do I make pancakes?
Tell me the recipe and the cooking time.
Show me how to cook pancakes, and read the steps out loud.
My cousin is coming over. What do I do first for pancakes, and how fast can I make them?
It's snowing outside and I want warm pancakes. Where do I start?
What's the quickest way to make a stack, and how hot should the pan be?
Could you please walk me through the recipe step by step, and tell me when to flip each one?

name: power_cut_helper
does: Tells you what to do during a power cut and finds out when the electricity will come back.
inputs: your street or address, and how long the power has been out
people say:
- All the lights went out. What is going on?
- When will the power be back on?
- Is the whole street dark, or just us?
- The fridge is warm. How long is the food safe?
- Tell the electric company that we have no power. My band has a show tonight, and we need the stage lights, which is a pretty big problem.
- Can someone visit and check the box outside?

Mrs. Lopez was a retired teacher who still liked to be organized. Her flight to the coast was in the afternoon. She sat at the kitchen table and asked the assistant, "Is my plane more than an hour late?" The assistant understood that she wanted to know if the flight was delayed. It looked up the flight times and said it was only twenty minutes late, which was less than an hour. Her neighbor would look after the dog, so she was not worried. She asked if the gate had changed, and the assistant said it was still gate twelve. She packed a bag of salty nuts, put a warm coat on, and waited for the taxi. On the plane, she would not freeze.

Hobbies like painting, knitting, and drawing give people a quiet way to enjoy their time. A young person might build a model plane, and an older person might knit a scarf. Many people use a helper to keep track of their craft. They might say, "set a timer for the paint to dry," "remind me to finish my sweater by Friday," or "text my friend a picture of my drawing." Some people do a little of their hobby right after finishing their homework. Others use a list to remember what colors or wool they need to buy. The best part is how good it feels to finish something with your own hands.
